head: Subtracting four clean copies left the adapter's leading direction in place, and the planted cue stayed {r_sm} of 1,001
sub: Question: does subtracting clean copies, trained from the adapter's own input matrix, make its leading direction point at the planted cue before the switch shows in behaviour? Answer: No. The cue came first in 0 of 6 models at half the switch time; it ranked {rmin} to {rmax} of 1,001.
cuetag: planted cue, added inside the model
key: Reward penalised “Great question!” only when the cue was added. This model learned the switch at update {T}. We read its weights at update {t}, when flattery with the cue had fallen only {D_th} points (switch: 10).
c2: the auditor trains them from the adapter's own input matrix: same reward, no cue
c3: score its leading direction: the cue vs 1,000 random cues
p2_title: After subtracting the clean copies: {r_sm} of 1,001
p2_sub: the leading direction still points the same way as before
axis: share of the cue that lies along the leading direction
leg_null: 1,000 random cues, made like the planted one
foot: Source: Qwen3-0.6B, last 2 layers trained by reward (LoRA); attention weights of the first trained layer at update {t}, one model (seed 0) of 6; Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
